newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MALDINI REFUSES TO CRITICISE HIS LACKLUSTRE TEAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MALDINI REFUSES TO CRITICISE HIS LACKLUSTRE TEAM.

text.p: Cesare Maldini may have suffered his first defeat as Italian coach but he refuses to blame the team for their lacklustre display against England.
England scored their first victory over Italy since 1977 on Wednesday, thanks to goals from Ian Wright and Paul Scholes.
Wright's goal after 26 minutes was the first Italy had conceded since Maldini took over from Arrigo Sacchi last December.
But there was no doubt that Italy played the game as if their minds were already on their summer holidays.
"I cannot criticise my team for anything," Maldini said.
"It is true were were tactically at fault for England's first goal and you cannot make mistakes like that against teams like England and expect to get away with them.

"But we are the end of a long, hard season and we have not had time to prepare properly for this tournament. I have some ideas in my head, some planning for the future but I don't think this is the time for me to try them with such an exhausted bunch of players."

Maldini's approach contrasts strongly with that of the English coach Glenn Hoddle, who has warmed to the idea of the Tournoi de France as a golden opportunity to experiment with new plans and tactics.
Hoddle also has the advantage that his players are at peak fitness and boosted by their World cup win over Poland on Saturday.
The mood in the England camp was extremely happy on Thursday but even though there is only prestige at stake in this tournament, there were signs of unrest among the Italians.
Some criticism was levelled against the Juventus players in the team for the poor showing against the English, which angered Juventus midfielder Angelo Di Livio.

"Everyone is always quick to blame the Juve players when something goes wrong," he said. "But there were a lot of players from other teams playing last night and perhaps they should ask themselves some questions."
Maldini is expected to make at least two changes -- and probably more -- for Italy's next match against Brazil in Lyon on Sunday.
Demetrio Albertini and Ciro Ferrara will both miss the match because of groin injuries but neither will go home for treatment just yet.
Alessandro Nesta, who replaced Ferrara at halftime on Wednesday, is expected to win his fifth cap against Brazil, while Christian Panucci of Real Madrid will take Di Livio's place in midfield.
